threads.body: @copilot Please change the assertions instead of opting these smoke tests into thread details. Remove this environment variable and explicitly assert that `thread.id` and `thread.name` are absent on both `GET /greeting` and `WebController.withSpan`, so the regular and AOT Spring Boot smoke tests exercise the new default-off behavior. The new autoconfiguration test already covers explicit opt-in; any additional installed-agent opt-in coverage should live in a focused test rather than the shared Spring Boot setup.

replies.body: Removed the shared thread-details environment override and added absence assertions for `thread.id` and `thread.name` on both spans. The focused Spring Boot smoke tests pass. Commit: `ea06541d`.

@copilot Please revise my earlier request and fix commit `ea06541def024e9e24da31fa9018842ab7a15a64`: remove both `doesNotContainKeys(THREAD_ID, THREAD_NAME)` assertion blocks from `AbstractSpringBootSmokeTest`, along with the unused thread-attribute imports. Keep the shared `OTEL_JAVAAGENT_ADD_THREAD_DETAILS` override removed; do not restore the old presence assertions or opt these smoke tests into thread details.

These general Spring Boot tests should not gain historical-absence checks merely because attributes previously emitted by default are now opt-in. This follows the intent of the supported-behavior testing guidance merged in #20438. Keep the focused `ThreadDetailsCustomizerProviderTest` cases for the changed default and explicit true/false settings: that remains supported configuration behavior. Leave production behavior and the rest of this PR unchanged; any clarification of the review rule belongs in a separate PR.
